<thought>To meet the constraints (≤ 5 steps, commercially available precursors, total cost < $10 000), the most direct disconnection is the ether bond that links the cyclohexane core to the conjugated diene side‑chain. Retrosynthetically this bond can be formed in one SN2‑type etherification between the primary alcohol of shikimic acid and the allylic bromide derived from sorbic acid. Both shikimic acid and sorbic acid are inexpensive, widely stocked chemicals, so the leaf nodes satisfy the buy‑ability requirement. The route therefore consists of a single retrosynthetic step.</thought>
